title: Ordering Food at a Restaurant
passage:
Peter and his mother were having dinner at Sunny Diner on Saturday night. The restaurant was busy, and they had to wait for a table.

"What would you like to eat tonight?" Mom asked, looking at the menu.

"I'd like to try the spaghetti," Peter said. "It looks more delicious than the fried rice."

"Good choice. I'd like to order the grilled chicken salad," Mom said. "It's healthier than the burger."

When the waiter came, Mom asked, "Could we also have some orange juice, please?"

"Sure," the waiter said with a smile. "Would you like anything else?"

"No, thank you. That's all for now," Mom said.

After a few minutes, the food arrived. The spaghetti was too hot to eat right away, so Peter waited and blew on it gently.

"Be careful," Mom reminded him. "Don't burn your tongue."

"This spaghetti tastes even better than the one at school," Peter said happily. "Can we come back next weekend?"

"Of course," Mom laughed. "If you finish your vegetables tonight, we can come back next Saturday."

Peter smiled and quickly ate his salad. The dinner was delicious, and they both felt full and happy. Before leaving, Peter thanked the waiter politely and said it was the best meal he had had in weeks.

vocab.example: I'd like to order the grilled chicken salad.
Mom asked, looking at the menu.
When the waiter came, Mom asked for some orange juice.
The spaghetti looks more delicious than the fried rice.
The salad is healthier than the burger.
Mom ordered the grilled chicken salad.
Mom reminded him to be careful.
Peter blew on the hot spaghetti gently.
After a few minutes, the food arrived.
If you finish your vegetables, we can come back next Saturday.
Good choice! The salad is a healthy choice.

grammar: 「Would like + to V」／「I'd like to...」：比 want 更委婉禮貌地表達「我想要」或提出請求，如 I'd like to try the spaghetti. / Would you like anything else?
形容詞比較級：單音節形容詞加 -er，多音節形容詞前加 more，用來比較兩者的差異，如 more delicious than、healthier than、even better than。
「too + 形容詞 + to + 原形動詞」：表示「太...而不能...」，如 The spaghetti was too hot to eat right away.

reading.q: Where did Peter and his mother have dinner?
reading.ex: 文章第一句提到他們星期六晚上在 Sunny Diner 吃晚餐。
Peter 說 "I'd like to try the spaghetti."，所以他點了義大利麵。
Mom 說她要點 grilled chicken salad（烤雞沙拉）。

reading.q: Why did Peter wait before eating the spaghetti?
reading.ex: 文中提到 the spaghetti was too hot to eat right away，所以他先等待並輕輕吹涼。

reading.q: What does Peter need to do so they can go back to the restaurant next Saturday?
reading.ex: Mom 說 "If you finish your vegetables tonight, we can come back next Saturday."

opts: I would like try the pizza.
I would like to try the pizza.
I would liked to try the pizza.
I would like trying the pizza.
grammar.ex: would like 後面要接「to + 原形動詞」，表示委婉地想要做某事，正確為 B。

grammar.q: This cake is ___ than that one. (delicious)
grammar.ex: delicious 是多音節形容詞，比較級要用 more + 形容詞，故為 more delicious。

opts: The soup was too hot drink.
The soup was too hot to drink.
The soup was so hot to drink.
The soup was too hot for drink.
grammar.ex: 「too + 形容詞 + to + 原形動詞」表示「太...而不能...」，正確用法為 too hot to drink。

grammar.q: What is the comparative form of "healthy"?
grammar.ex: 形容詞字尾為「子音+y」時，比較級要去 y 加 ier，healthy → healthier。

grammar.q: Which sentence politely means "I want to order a salad"?
opts: I'd like to order a salad.
I liking to order a salad.
I like ordering a salad very.
grammar.ex: 「I'd like to + 原形動詞」是禮貌地表達「我想要」的正確句型。

vocab.ex: menu 意思是「菜單」，顧客用它來選擇餐點。
politely 是副詞，意思是「禮貌地」，如 Peter thanked the waiter politely.

vocab.q: The soup was too hot, so I blew on it ___.
vocab.ex: 修飾動詞 blew 需用副詞 gently（溫和地），而非形容詞 gentle。
remind 意思是「提醒」，如 Mom reminded him to be careful.
arrive 意思是「到達」，如 the food arrived after a few minutes.
